24 Oct: Visualizer FX V.17: water blend modes, Blend at the top, a draggable settings panel. Live (CR-165, your LATER line "more blend modes for the water layer, like dissolve, displace, etc." and your follow-up). Seven blends now: Add, Dissolve, Multiply (decks show through the water), Difference, Overlay, Luma key (decks cut out by the water light) and Displace (the water bends the decks, like refraction). The Blend choice is in the always-visible strip at the top of settings, under the Scene mix; Scene mix is the strength for all of them. Drag the thin grip on the settings panel left edge to widen it (double-click for the default); wider than about 560 px the levels sit two to a row. The Scene tab is split into Scene layer, Ceiling and floor and Scene settings, and the old Mix section on Show is now Trails and beat. Not checked: how Displace and Luma key look over a real song and projector; the strength is a first guess to tune by eye. The camera is not blended with the water.

24 Oct: Visualizers page. Live (CR-164, said in-session). The sixteen visualizer versions are off the Image tools page and on their own page, Visualizers, opened from one door on Image tools (newest first, the current build badged, a back button to Image tools). Image tools also keeps a door straight into the current build. Not checked: I cannot enter a band password, so I saw the page with its login hidden.

24 Oct: Visualizer FX V.16 now has an Idle on/off button. Live (CR-162, said in-session, replacing my first fix). The jump back to Water was the idle mode, which is a separate switch from Auto and was buried in the Sound tab. There is now an Idle pill in the top bar beside Auto and an Idle button in the live strip at the top of settings: tap to turn idle off (a picture already idle comes straight back) and on again. Auto is left as it was. Not checked: your pad and a real gap between songs.

24 Oct: Visualizer FX V.16: the scene settings have their own Scene tab, and the three mixes are always at the top. Live (CR-161, said in-session). Settings now has Show, Camera, Scene, Stage, Sound, Help. Everything for the water (on/off, the five scenes, blend, ceiling and floor lines, all the engine controls, reset) is in Scene; the big water block above the tabs is gone. Under White and Black there are now Decks (the crossfader), Camera and Scene sliders, with a Water button that turns the layer on and off. On the look: V.15 and V.14 are identical at default settings and share saved settings, and V.15 added a preview where any click moved a ceiling or floor line, which changes how the water and creatures behave. That is fixed: a line only moves when you grab it, and there is a Reset ceiling and floor button. If your V.15 water still looks worse, press Reset all scene settings in the Scene tab and tell me. Not checked: your machine.

Not a live-site change. Not checked: a real handoff from your other machine, so tell me where it snags.

23 Oct: Visualizer FX V.15: the Scene layer is a proper layer now. Live (CR-159, you could not find the ceiling and floor lines and saw little use in it). In the Show tab under Scene layer there is a preview with two lines to drag: where the ceiling starts (down from the top) and where the floor starts (up from the bottom). Below it, every setting the water engine has (negative space, room perspective, look, bubbles, creatures, level, line art, resolution), resting levels for the routed ones, and a Blend choice: Add over the decks, or Dissolve, where the decks fade out as it rises so the water can carry a scene on its own. Settings are saved for the venue and Reset puts them back. Not checked: how the ceiling looks on a real wall.

23 Oct: Visualizer FX V.14: negative space is now part of the animations, not a blob over them. Live (CR-158, you said the void just hid the picture). The floating mask is gone. Void now sets how much of each scene is left black, in that scene’s own shape: columns cut through Cosmic Wave and Waves, petals and a hollow centre in Kaleidoscope, black wedges through the tunnels, plasma blobs hollowed into rings, stars in lanes, grid cells emptied, a black eye in Vortex. Void 0 is the old look; a kick still closes it a little. V.13 kept on the menu.

Checked with a simulated pad, not your DualSense.

22 Oct: Visualizer FX is now V.8 and makes room for black. Live (CR-149, said in-session). A new Void slider in the Show tab (default 0.35, kept in presets) lets slow dark patches open up in the picture, and every effect edges them in its own pattern: dots shrink, lines thin out, stripes fade, colour channels close together. A kick shrinks the void so the picture returns on the beat; it stays out of your stage-target rings and is off in idle. The scenes also leave more empty space (shorter trails, fewer layers and blobs). Effect 5 (CMYK) now draws light on black like the others instead of dark on light. Presets saved earlier load with no void. V.7 is kept on the menu. Checked in the browser, not on a real projector over a band: how much void suits is yours to judge, and Void 0 was not compared pixel for pixel with V.7. That finishes the wish list.

22 Oct: Visualizer FX V.5 has a Streak tunnel scene. Live (CR-150, said in-session). Long lines stream out of a vanishing point, short and thin near it and long and thick at the edge. It warps like the other tunnels (right trigger and bass stretch and twist the lines, left trigger sways the point) and follows Line width. The point is stepped from the controller: Share (the small button by the touchpad), the / key, or MIDI note 73 moves it centre, left, right, up, down and round, gliding each time. It is the last scene in the list. Checked with the keyboard and a virtual pad, not a real DualSense: if Chrome keeps Share for itself on your machine, use the key or MIDI. Next: Stage targets (CR-146), then Negative space (CR-149).

22 Oct: Visualizer FX V.5 tunnels now warp instead of pulse, and there is a Line width slider. Live (CR-145). Tunnel, Tunnel Rush and Vortex no longer jerk when the bass or the speed changes: everything that drives them glides over about a quarter of a second, and ring size and brightness stay steady. The right trigger and the bass twist the rings and stretch them into ovals; the left trigger sways the vanishing point; a kick leans it briefly instead of flashing. Line width (Show tab, 0.3 to 3 times) thickens or thins the lines in those three and in Waves, Grid and Cosmic Wave, and is saved in presets. Checked on a simulated clock and a virtual pad. Still yours: how strong the warp feels with a real DualSense and music, and whether the Tunnel Rush rings, now a fixed size, read as steady rather than static. Next: your long-lines tunnel with a toggled vanishing point (CR-150), then Stage targets (CR-146) and Negative space (CR-149).

20 Oct: Visualizer FX V.5 has an Auto switch, a list of what auto can use, and an Auto speed slider. Live (CR-144). The buttons at the top now sit below the banner on the control screen so the new pill fits. Not checked: real music through a mic (beats came from the demo pulse) and the DualSense. 19 Oct: Visualizer FX V.5 now goes idle between songs. Live (CR-143). In the Sound tab, Idle watches the real sound level (not the auto level, which lifted a quiet room back up) and, once it has stayed under the mark you set for 4 seconds with nobody on the controls, fades both decks to the Water scene and stops the sound moving the picture. Any key, button or stick, or the music coming back, wakes it at once. With no audio connected it does the same, so a fresh load settles onto the water. You choose the idle scene and the idle effect (keep the current one, any of the eight, or a saved preset), and Preview idle shows it on demand. Two fixes on the way: automated mode used to cancel itself after ten seconds with no controller connected and now drifts gently as intended, and Water is brighter and livelier while idle so it shows through halftone. Not checked: a real room and mic, so set the white mark by eye while a song plays and between songs (the 2 percent default is a guess); the DualSense; the projector; how effects other than halftone and raw look over the idle water.

19 Oct: Visualizer FX V.5 Plasma now answers the controls and no longer sits still. Live (CR-142). Before, it only listened to the bass and mids, ran at a third speed whenever you were not touching anything, and was a few huge blobs overlapping into one wash, so the triggers, Speed, Complexity, Colour speed and Spin did nothing to it. Now R2 swells and brightens it, L2 swirls it and sends a warp wave through the blobs, kicks pulse it and step its colour on, the mids widen it and (through Complexity) add blobs, the highs brighten a small satellite on each blob, and Speed, Colour speed and Spin set its pace and colour. It drifts at two thirds pace even when untouched. A Plasma block in the Help tab lists these. Water also follows the Pulse slider now. Checked with simulated input: R2 nearly doubles the brightness, L2 triples the movement, sound and kicks drive it; all eight effects over it and the fallback drawing. Not checked: how it feels on your pad and with the band; at rest it is dimmer than the old wash on purpose (smaller blobs leave room to move), so say if you want it brighter. Next: Idle between songs (CR-143).

11 Oct: Saved presets for Visualizer FX, with download, upload and Snalbum sync. Live (CR-133). The effects 1 to 8 are the first presets, and anything you save is added after them (9, 10 and so on): swap with the number keys (9 and 0 reach the first two), the stick clicks (they step through effects and presets in one ring), or the buttons, and tick them in Limit what the controller can reach like any effect. A saved preset keeps the effect, its sliders, both decks' scenes and hues, crossfade, trails, colour behaviour, pulse and glitch, and the sound routing if you switch that on; it swaps in over about a second, and choosing a plain effect afterwards puts the sliders back as they were. You name, move, update (the circular arrow), delete and download each one in the Saved presets box on the Show tab; Download all and Upload move them as a file. An offline copy carries your presets and keeps them in that browser, so a look made offline goes up later by uploading the file on the Snalbum page. On Snalbum a preset is sent to the site when you create, rename, update, delete, reorder or upload one, once you are signed in as site admin (sign in on the Snalbum menu page in the same tab, or type the admin password in the box under the list); until then it stays on that device. One thing differs from what you asked: it uses the site's own settings table, the same one that keeps your tools menu order, not a storage bucket, because a bucket needs a deploy I could not do from here. Checked: swapping, ordering, limits, file download and upload, an offline copy with its presets, and the whole sync against a pretend server (new, reorder, delete, wrong password, a second laptop's changes). Not checked: a real save to the site, which needs your admin password, so the first real save is when you sign in; and the file picker and download in your own browser.

11 Oct: Visualizer FX, a new tool beside the Visualizer (Tools menu, and the Image tools page as its last door). Live. It runs the Visualizer's picture through halftone, stipple, line displacement, RGB and CMYK displacement, high contrast black and white or dazzle camo, dissolving from one effect to the next with a small colour lift that settles back. It is black and white and ambient until played: colour only arrives on a bar line or a big bass hit (or X by hand), and with nobody on the controls for ten seconds the controller's parameters drift on their own until someone touches them. Camera (switched on from the settings or with K, never from the controller): the right stick moves the mix and it stays where you leave it. Aimed at the band it tracks movement rather than light, since the projector is lighting the stage: what moves is lifted and outlined whole, the show's own flicker and any frame-sized change is ignored, and Auto balance tunes it to the stage's flicker. Movement also nudges the show for a moment (a little colour, a slight push-in) and it settles back when the stage is still, and a slider on the laptop sets how much the camera's position steers the effects. Every part of it, and a full set of picture controls, is a slider on the laptop, laid out in tabs (Show, Camera, Stage, Sound, Help) under a strip of the live buttons, with folding groups, an i hint on each and double-click to reset a slider. The controller is six controls, smoothed so the hands and the music read as one gesture: left stick rotates and sets the scale (which stays where it is left), right stick splits the effect, RT pushes, LT warps. A and B change scenes, the stick clicks step the effects, and blackout and freeze are laptop-only. Strobe (R on the laptop) is not on the audience pad at all: each firing is 10 percent dimmer than the last until 5 seconds go by with no strobe, and a run fades out and switches itself off within 5 seconds. Its flash rate is 10 a second on the clock, which is above the usual photosensitivity guidance of about 3, so put a warning up at the venue or ask me to lower it. It rumbles with the bass, uses the tilt of a PlayStation pad over USB, and a kick stutters the last few frames back over the picture. Projector: the projector button sends only the picture fullscreen to the second screen, the settings stay on the laptop, and Audience control decides whether the controller is heard. The settings can limit the controller to certain effects, down to one. Checked on the live site with simulated input: all eight effects, the camera and the tracker (a walking body lit whole, flicker and a frame-sized sweep ignored, stillness fading out), the glitch, rumble, tilt, automated mode and the held scale, with no console errors. Not checked: a real second screen or projector, a real camera, pad, mic or MIDI device, Chrome's first-time permission prompts, and whether the tracking holds up on your own stage lights. If it misfires there, the Movement sliders and Auto balance are where to dial it in.

24 Sep — Playback seems to ‘shuffle’ rather than play in order on music player haven’t tested this behavior in release view yet <snalbum <music library
Fixed and live (CR-121). It was never shuffle. Two orders had drifted apart: the player advanced through the raw list the server sends back, while the page draws your folders first with their songs inside and the loose songs last. Those only agree when nothing is in a folder. On Lakehorse, finishing “Elevator” jumped to the top of the page, and finishing a song inside Demos jumped out to a live set and back. On Dando it was worse, because its folder order runs the opposite way to its song order: starting from the first row on screen, playback reached 11 of your 27 songs and then stopped, silently skipping the other 16. Both orders now come from one place, so next is always the row underneath. Songs in a collapsed folder stay in the running order on purpose, otherwise the order would change as you open and shut folders. Shuffle itself is untouched. Two more turned up in the same function while reading it, neither biting you yet: a song that also sits in a music folder would have vanished from release view entirely, which is the view you said you had not tested, and moving from a band library into a shared link kept the previous band’s folder headings. Both fixed. No database change. Checked against the deployed file with your real libraries: the running order matches the screen, every song appears once, next is the row below from all 23 Lakehorse starting points, a full play-through reaches all 27 Dando songs, and shuffle still covers everything. One gap, yours if you want it closed: I loaded the page cold and it came up clean, but I do not type passwords into login fields, so nobody has watched it play through behind your login. Press play on the top row of a Dando folder and it should walk straight down the page.

9 Sep — paint module should not show up until ‘draw over this’ is clicked <paint <art
Fixed and live, as part of CR-116 below — same bug. The toolbar’s hidden state was set with the DOM hidden attribute, but the module’s own stylesheet also set display:flex unconditionally, and an author stylesheet rule always beats the browser’s built-in hidden-means-display-none rule, whatever the selector. So it never actually hid, on either page. Switched to a class toggle instead. Confirmed idle-hidden on both Art Concepts and the Band artwork page.
